authority.statement: This packet records adversarial parser, differential, delegated-verifier, and bounded-fuzz evidence. It grants no call-site migration or dependency-cutover authority.

provenance.subject: C=US, ST=Test, L=Test, O=AsuperSync Test, CN=localhost

provenance.key_reuse_boundary: The pre-existing test-only RSA key is reused solely to make compact deterministic-chain fixtures. This is not production key guidance.
commands: openssl req -new -key tests/fixtures/tls/server.key -subj /CN=Asupersync A5 Constrained Root -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:0 -addext keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign -addext nameConstraints=critical,permitted;DNS:.allowed.example
openssl req/x509 leaf recipes use fixed serials 0xA502 and 0xA503, CA signing, CA:FALSE, digitalSignature plus keyEncipherment, serverAuth, and exact DNS SANs
openssl req/x509 wildcard recipe uses fixed serial 0xA504, self-signing, CA:FALSE, digitalSignature plus keyEncipherment, serverAuth, and DNS:*.example.com

provenance.determinism: Every recipe is pure bytes with fixed tags, lengths, OIDs, values, and mutation offsets.

provenance.oracle_policy: Seeds are raw bytes or PEM certificates only. The fuzz target asserts determinism and bounded errors, never an incumbent accept/reject oracle.

differential_contract.x509_parser_scope: Structural acceptance is compared only after requiring one complete certificate and empty remainder. Signature, trust, time, name, wildcard, constraints, EKU/KU admission, and revocation are excluded.
differential_contract.delegated_scope: rustls/WebPKI owns chain signatures, trust anchors, time, DNS wildcard matching, and name constraints. Local exact-pin policy owns the approved facts after standard-first UnknownIssuer fallback.
intentional_differential_divergences: der_min rejects duplicate extension OIDs even when x509-parser can structurally decode them
the pinned-leaf profile rejects critical extensions outside its KU, SAN, and EKU allow-set
der_min emits time, EKU, KU, SAN, and BasicConstraints facts without applying caller policy

assertions: same bytes and profile produce an identical result
every error offset is at most input length
numeric observed and limit detail never exceed the certificate cap
PEM extraction is input-size bounded and certificate-count bounded
forbidden_oracles: filesystem access from the fuzz callback
fuzz_contract.resource_claim: The target demonstrates bounded parser behavior only under the recorded max_len, corpus, elapsed run, and process RSS receipt. It is not a throughput or exhaustive-security proof.

rollback_triggers: any unexplained accept/reject divergence inside the normalized complete-DER overlap
any generated fixture whose recorded fingerprint, validity, serial, or extension set drifts
any fuzz crash, panic, hang, out-of-bounds offset, or unbounded numeric detail
any fuzz target oracle dependency on x509-parser or rustls/WebPKI
any critical-extension policy broader than the approved A3 profile contract
any delegated wildcard or name-constraint case that no longer fails closed

downstream_handoff.scope: A6 may use this A5 corpus as regression evidence while serially migrating call sites. A5 itself grants no migration authority.

no_claim_boundaries: no x509-parser dependency-removal or cutover claim
no runtime behavior change outside test-only fixtures and fuzzing
no exhaustive certificate-language or security proof
